strengths: Addresses practical efficiency problem in emerging diffusion LLM models with training-free approach
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (LLaDA, Dream, LLaDA-V) and diverse benchmarks with extensive ablation studies
Well-motivated technical approach with empirical observation of high KV activation similarity (Figure 3) and clear identification of parallel decoding degradation root cause
Impressive speedup results (up to 27.6×) with minimal accuracy loss (1-2 points), demonstrated across text and multimodal tasks
Theorem 1 provides formal theoretical justification for confidence-based parallel decoding with explicit divergence bounds
Clear presentation with informative visualizations and detailed appendix including qualitative analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: KV caching is well-established; confidence-based selection is incremental over LLaDA's top-K approach
Theoretical contribution is modest: Theorem 1 assumes well-defined joint PMF that MDMs may not satisfy; worst-case bounds are loose and restrictive condition (n+1)ε≤1 may not hold in practice
KV Cache approximation lacks depth: fundamentally breaks down for multimodal LLaDA-V (accuracy drops >8% with small blocks, requiring different refresh strategy), suggesting unaddressed limitations
Scalability concerns underexplored: LLaDA throughput plateaus at batch size ~8 (Figure 9), severely limiting practical deployment; compute-bound nature of diffusion models acknowledged but not solved

Experimental design issues: headline '27.6×' speedup uses atypical conditions (8-shot + 1024 tokens); modest 5-8× speedups for standard 256-token generation; limited batch-size analysis; weak baselines (mostly method variants, no comparison with other acceleration techniques)

Confidence-based decoding lacks principled design: threshold (0.9) appears ad-hoc with non-trivial sensitivity (Figure 5); 'always unmask max confidence' fallback is a hack; factor-based strategy trades 1-3% accuracy for throughput gains without clear characterization
Insufficient baseline comparisons: only 2 AR models in one setting (Figure 1a); no comparison with other acceleration methods (quantization, pruning, distillation) or alternative inference approaches
Limited analysis of failure modes and accuracy-efficiency trade-offs: no investigation of task/token-type sensitivity; missing characterization of when method is not recommended
